title: Pushes and Pulls
question: How can I make my toy cart go, stop or turn?

steps.title: Push or pull
steps.text: This toy cart sits still on the play mat. It will not move by itself. To make it move, you have to push it or pull it. A push moves it away from you. A pull brings it toward you. The big arrow shows which way the push or pull goes.
steps.try: Press Push, then press Pull. Watch which way the arrow points.
steps.see: When you push, the cart rolls away from you. When you pull the string, the cart rolls toward you. The cart always moves the way the arrow points.

steps.title: Small push, big push
steps.text: Now let's push the cart from the start square. First a small push, then a big push. The numbers on the mat help us see how far the cart goes.
steps.try: Press Small push. Then press Big push. Count the squares each time.
steps.see: After a small push the cart stops close by. After a big push it goes faster and rolls much farther. A bigger push makes a bigger change.

steps.title: Push to stop
steps.text: A push can start something moving, and a push can also stop it. Here the cart is rolling fast. To stop it, push against the way it is going.
steps.try: Press Roll it, then press Push to stop while the cart is still rolling.
steps.see: The stop arrow points the other way from where the cart is going. The cart slows down and stops right away, long before it would stop by itself.

steps.title: Bounce off a wall
steps.text: Here is a ball and a wall. When the ball hits the wall, the wall pushes back on the ball. That push turns the ball around, so it rolls back the other way.
steps.try: Press Roll it gently, then press Roll it hard.
steps.see: The ball always comes back after it hits the wall. A hard roll bounces back faster and farther than a gentle roll.

steps.title: Push from the side
steps.text: A push does not only make things go faster or slower. A push from the side can turn a moving ball, so it goes a new way. The dots show the path the ball takes.
steps.try: Press Roll the ball, then press Side push while it is rolling.
steps.see: The ball rolls in a straight line until the side push. Then its path bends and it goes off in a new direction.

steps.title: Roll down a ramp
steps.text: On a ramp, nobody has to push the cart. The Earth pulls everything down. We call this pull gravity. Gravity pulls the cart down the ramp. On a higher ramp, the cart goes faster at the bottom.
steps.try: Press Low ramp and then High ramp. Each time the cart lets go at the top.
steps.see: From the low ramp the cart stops after a short roll. From the high ramp it comes down faster and rolls much farther across the mat.

quiz.q: You give a toy car a big push instead of a small push. What happens?
quiz.why: A bigger push makes a bigger change. The car goes faster, so it rolls farther before it stops.

quiz.q: How can you stop a rolling ball?
options: Push it the same way it is going
Push against the way it is going
quiz.why: A push against the way something is moving slows it down and can stop it.

quiz.q: A ball rolls into a wall and comes back. Why?
quiz.why: When the ball hits the wall, the wall pushes back on it. That push turns the ball around.
